title: 13th Annual HPR New Year's Eve Show
blurb: The HPR community gathers for a 26-hour marathon chat covering infrastructure updates, 3D printing projects, and the challenges of modern car maintenance.

summary.purpose: To celebrate the New Year and discuss the technical evolution and infrastructure of the Hacker Public Radio platform.

keyTakeaways.point: HPR is transitioning to a distributed Content Delivery Network model with mirrors in multiple countries to ensure availability during Internet Archive outages.
The HPR website has moved to a static site model to significantly reduce server load and operational costs.
Long-time contributor Dave is retiring from his role as 'janitor,' necessitating a transition in how show notes and transcoding are managed.
New show ground rules emphasize push-to-talk and avoiding dead air to simplify the post-production process for the marathon recording.

topics.heading: HPR Infrastructure and CDN
points: Implementation of a peer-to-peer rsync script to mirror audio files across multiple global locations.
Use of a round-robin load balancer to distribute traffic between the Internet Archive and private mirrors.
Transitioning to static HTML pages to eliminate expensive database queries during peak traffic.

topics.heading: Show Production and Automation
points: Challenges with transcoding scripts breaking due to library updates in Fedora 41.
Introduction of a new WYSIWYG editor for show notes to reduce manual formatting work for administrators.
Preserving metadata across different audio formats when uploading to the Internet Archive.

topics.heading: Hardware and DIY Projects
points: Joe's project to 3D print a 10-inch server rack for Raspberry Pis and networking gear.
Discussion on repairing Bluetooth neckband headphones and the limitations of true wireless earbuds.
Ken's 'hacker desk' setup using garden mesh, IKEA hooks, and velcro for cable management.

topics.heading: Community and Social Media
points: Higher engagement levels on Mastodon compared to Twitter for HPR show announcements.
The history of the New Year's show, which expanded to 26 hours to cover all global time zones.
Debate over return-to-office policies and their impact on productivity and employee retention.

nextSteps: Release the marathon recording mid-year during a submission lull.
Continue testing the community CDN and adding more mirrors in the Netherlands and at ISPs.
Finalize the transition of administrative tasks from Dave to the remaining team.

actionItems.text: Update the HPR origin server drive from 1TB to 4TB.
Rewrite the transcoding scripts to fix library compatibility issues on Fedora 41.
Find a volunteer to manage the Community News project following Dave's retirement.
